title: fetch_peer_blob: content_type query parameter incompletely percent-encoded
description: In peer_fetch.rs::fetch_peer_blob (line 350), ct_encoded only replaces '/' and '+'. An attacker-controlled content_type (per the trust boundary table in CLAUDE.md) containing '&', '=', '#', or '?' would corrupt the query string. For example, content_type='image/png&x=y' produces '?accept=image%2Fpng&x=y', injecting an extra query parameter. A '#' would truncate the URL at the fragment boundary. The fix is to use full percent-encoding on the ct value (encode all chars except unreserved), consistent with how percent_encode_path_segment handles the filename. The content_type is also used directly as a header value (line 391), where Hyper validates and rejects CRLF, so no header injection is possible, but the query string is not validated.
